speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your infant has been vomiting bile and cannot pass meconium, which is concerning. To determine the cause of this obstruction, can you tell me exactly how many days old the baby is now?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Atresia (likely Duodenal Atresia or Jejunal/Ileal Atresia). The history of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium in a 2-day-old infant, and abdominal distension is highly suggestive of a proximal bowel obstruction, likely atresia given the home birth and lack of polyhydramnios history (which would be noted if the mother had excessive amniotic fluid). An abdominal X-ray is urgently required to confirm the presence of a "double bubble" sign or other obstruction patterns. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray
